definitions.explanation: A family that has separated from the main household to establish its own independent household. The opposite of the main family (honke).

definitions.gloss: the act of establishing a branch family; branching off
definitions.explanation: The process of a family member leaving the main household to start a separate family line.

examples.japanese: うち⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{本家|ほんけ}→本家：13087_honke⟧⟦ではなく→ではなく：09578_dehanaku⟧{分家|ぶんけ}だ。
examples.english: Our family is a branch family, not the main family.

examples.japanese: {分家|ぶんけ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧たち⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{正月|しょうがつ}→正月：01433_shougatsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{本家|ほんけ}→本家：13087_honke⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{集|あつ}まる→集まる：01162_atsumaru⟧。
examples.english: People from the branch families also gather at the main house for New Year's.

examples.japanese: ⟦{祖父|そふ}→祖父：01452_sofu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{代|だい}→〜代：28331_dai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{本家|ほんけ}→本家：13087_honke⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧{分家|ぶんけ}⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: We branched off from the main family in my grandfather's generation.

examples.japanese: ⟦{次男|じなん}→次男：13210_jinan⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{分家|ぶんけ}⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{新|あたら}しい→新しい：00506_atarashii⟧⟦{家|いえ}→家：00612_ie⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{建|た}てた→建てる：01189_tateru⟧。
examples.english: The second son branched off and built a new house.

examples.japanese: ⟦{江戸時代|えどじだい}→江戸時代：20431_edojidai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{武家|ぶけ}→武家：13242_buke⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{分家|ぶんけ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{厳|きび}しい→厳しい：01125_kibishii⟧⟦{規則|きそく}→規則：01382_kisoku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦あった→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: In the Edo period, there were strict rules even for branching off from samurai families.

notes:
Composed of ⟦{分|ぶん}→分：26216_bun⟧ (divide, separate) + {家|け} (house, family). Central to the traditional Japanese family system ({家制度|いえせいど}).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {分家|ぶんけ}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to establish a branch family
- ⟦{本家|ほんけ}→本家：13087_honke⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{分家|ぶんけ}: main family and branch family
- {分家|ぶんけ}{筋|すじ}: branch family line

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{本家|ほんけ}→本家：13087_honke⟧: main family, head family — the original household from which branch families separate
- {別家|べっけ}: separate household — similar meaning but less common
- ⟦{宗家|そうけ}→宗家：22013_souke⟧: head family (of an artistic/martial arts school) — specifically the founding lineage of a traditional school

CULTURAL NOTE:
In the traditional Japanese family system, the eldest son typically inherited the main household (⟦{本家|ほんけ}→本家：13087_honke⟧), while younger sons would {分家|ぶんけ} and establish their own households. Though the legal {家制度|いえせいど} was abolished after World War II, the concepts of ⟦{本家|ほんけ}→本家：13087_honke⟧ and {分家|ぶんけ} remain culturally significant, especially in rural areas. The term is also used metaphorically for businesses or organizations that have split from a parent entity.
